label: lem: feasibility
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: \emph{Feasibility

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $g(u)=(C_Tu-x_f)^\top\Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}(C_Tu-x_f)$. The constraint in \eqref{eq: meci} is feasible if and only if
$\gamma\ge \underset{u}{\min}\: g(u)\triangleq \underline{\gamma}_{T}^{\text{(nor)}}$. Note that $\underline{\gamma}_{T}^{\text{(nor)}}$ is the projection error of $x_f$ on Range$(C_T)$ with respect to the $\Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}$ weighted norm. The corresponding projection matrix is given by $ P = C_T(C_T^\top \Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}C_T)^\dagger C_T^\top \Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}.$
Then, we have
\begin{align*}
\underline{\gamma}_{T}^{\text{(nor)}}
&=
(x_f-P x_f)^\top
\Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}
(x_f-Px_f) \\
&=
x_f^\top
(I-P)^\top
\Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}
(I-P)x_f 
=
x_f^\top
\Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}
(I-P)x_f, 
\end{align*}
where the last equality follows from  the symmetryidempotence ($P^2=P$) and self-adjointness ($P^\top\Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}= \Sigma_{e_T}^{-1}P$) of $P$.
Substituting $P$, we get the result. 
\qed

label: thm: optimal_cost
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: \emph{Optimal Solution

label: eq:lagrangian
title: Proof
head: environment

label: prop: monotonicity
title: Proposition
body_md: \label{prop: monotonicity} Let $J_T^* = u_T^{*\top} Q_T u_T^*$ be the optimal cost of Problem \eqref{eq: meci}. Then, if $A\Sigma_{0}A^\top + \Sigma \succeq \Sigma_{0}$, we have $J_{T+1}^* \leq  J_{T}^*$ for all $T\geq 1$.
head: environment
name: \emph{Decrease of $J_T^*$ with $T$

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider QCQP \eqref{eq: meci} at time $T+1$ with input $u_{T+1} = \begin{bmatrix}
    u_T^{*\top} & 0
    \end{bmatrix}^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{m(T+1)}$. Then, we have 
    \begin{align*}
         &(C_{T+1}u_{T+1}-x_f)^\top \Sigma_{e_{T+1}}^{-1}(C_{T+1}u_{T+1}-x_f) \\ 
         &= (C_Tu_T^* - x_f)^\top (A\Sigma_{e_T}A^\top + \Sigma)^{-1}(C_Tu_T^*-x_f)
    \end{align*}
Hence, if $A\Sigma_{e_T}A^\top + \Sigma \succeq \Sigma_{e_T}$ i.e. $A^T(A \Sigma_0 A^\top + \Sigma -\Sigma_0)(A^T)^\top \succeq 0 \Leftrightarrow A \Sigma_0 A^\top + \Sigma \succeq \Sigma_0$, $u_{T+1}$ is feasible at time $T+1$ which implies
$J(u_{T+1}^*) \leq J(u_{T+1}) = u_{T+1}^\top Q_{T+1} u_{T+1} = u_{T}^{*\top} Q_{T} u_{T}^* 
= J(u_T^*)$.
This completes the proof.
\qed
head: environment

label: thm:horizon_limit
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: \emph{Convergence of Optimal Cost

label: eq: J_lim
title: Proof
body_md:
Define $G_T
\triangleq
C_TQ_T^{-1}C_T^\top,$
$\widetilde\Sigma_0
\triangleq
P^{-1}\Sigma_0P^{-\top},$ $\widetilde G_T
\triangleq P^{-1}G_TP^{-\top},$ $\widetilde{M}_T
\triangleq
P^{-1}\Sigma_{e_T}P^{-\top},$
\begin{align*}
\widetilde S_T(\nu)
&\triangleq
P^{-1}S_T(\nu)P^{-\top}
\triangleq
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathcal A_T(\nu) & \mathcal B_T(\nu)\\
\mathcal B_T(\nu)^\top & \mathcal D_T(\nu)
\end{bmatrix}, \text{and} \nonumber\\
\widetilde z_T
&\triangleq
\begin{bmatrix}
z_{n,T}^\top & z_{s,T}^\top
\end{bmatrix}^{\top}
=
\widetilde S_T(\nu_T)^{-1}
\begin{bmatrix}
(x_f^n)^\top & (x_f^s)^\top
\end{bmatrix}^{\top}
\\
&=
\begin{bmatrix}
\mathcal A_T^{-1}x_f^n
-
\mathcal A_T^{-1}\mathcal B_T
\mathcal H_T^{-1}
\left(
x_f^s-\mathcal B_T^\top\mathcal A_T^{-1}x_f^n
\right)
\\[3mm]
\mathcal H_T^{-1}
\left(
x_f^s-\mathcal B_T^\top\mathcal A_T^{-1}x_f^n
\right)
\end{bmatrix},
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal H_T(\nu)
\triangleq
\mathcal D_T(\nu)
-
\mathcal B_T(\nu)^\top
\mathcal A_T(\nu)^{-1}
\mathcal B_T(\nu).$
We then re-write optimal cost as 
\begin{align}
J_T^*
&=
z_{n,T}^\top G_{nn,T}z_{n,T}
+
2z_{n,T}^\top G_{ns,T}z_{s,T}
+
z_{s,T}^\top G_{ss,T}z_{s,T}.
\label{eq: J_lim}
\end{align}
Using Lemma~\ref{lem:block_separation}, for every fixed $\nu>0$, $\mathcal H_T(\nu)
\to
W_c^s+\frac{1}{\nu}W_w^s,$ $\mathcal B_T(\nu)^\top
\mathcal A_T(\nu)^{-1}x_f^n
\to0.$
Therefore, $z_{s,T}(\nu)
\to
z_{s,\infty}(\nu)
\triangleq
\left(
W_c^s+\frac{1}{\nu}W_w^s
\right)^{-1}x_f^s.$

Since $M_{nn,T}\preceq \nu\mathcal A_T(\nu)$, with
$\mathcal A_T(\nu)^{-1}\to0$,
$\|\mathcal A_T(\nu)^{-1/2}\mathcal B_T(\nu)\|\to0$, and
$z_{s,T}$ is bounded, we obtain
\[
z_{n,T}^\top M_{nn,T}z_{n,T}
\le
\nu\left\|
\mathcal A_T(\nu)^{-1/2}
\bigl(x_f^n-\mathcal B_T(\nu)z_{s,T}\bigr)
\right\|^2
\to0.
\]
Further, since $\widetilde{M}_T\succeq0$, we have $|z_{n,T}^\top M_{ns,T}z_{s,T}|^2
\le
(z_{n,T}^\top M_{nn,T}z_{n,T})
(z_{s,T}^\top M_{ss,T}z_{s,T}),$ and hence
$z_{n,T}^\top M_{ns,T}z_{s,T}\to0.$
Therefore, for every fixed $\nu>0$,
\begin{align*}
f_T(\nu)
&=
\frac{1}{\nu^2}
z_T(\nu)^\top M_Tz_T(\nu)
\nonumber\\
&=
\frac{1}{\nu^2}
\Big(
z_{n,T}^\top M_{nn,T}z_{n,T}
+
2z_{n,T}^\top M_{ns,T}z_{s,T}
\\&+
z_{s,T}^\top M_{ss,T}z_{s,T}
\Big)
\nonumber\\
&\to
\frac{1}{\nu^2}
z_{s,\infty}(\nu)^\top
W_w^s
z_{s,\infty}(\nu)
\nonumber\\
&=
x_f^{s\top}
(W_w^s+\nu W_c^s)^{-1}
W_w^s
(W_w^s+\nu W_c^s)^{-1}
x_f^s 
= f_\infty(\nu),
\label{eq:f_block_expansion}
\end{align*}
where the last equality follows from $z_{s,\infty}(\nu)
=
\nu
(W_w^s+\nu W_c^s)^{-1}x_f^s.$
Hence, $f_\infty(\nu)$ is continuous and strictly decreasing, with $\lim_{\nu\to0}f_\infty(\nu)
=
(x_f^s)^\top(W_w^s)^{-1}x_f^s
=
\gamma_\infty,$ and $\lim_{\nu\to\infty}f_\infty(\nu)=0.$
Therefore, for $0<\gamma<\gamma_\infty$, using monotonicity of
$f_\infty$ and uniqueness of $\nu_T^*$, we obtain
$\nu_T\to\nu_\infty$ and $z_{s,T}\to
(S_\infty^s)^{-1}x_f^s.$

We next consider other terms in optimal cost. Since
$G_{nn,T}\preceq\mathcal A_T(\nu_T),$ we get $z_{n,T}^\top G_{nn,T}z_{n,T}\to0.$
Moreover, since $\widetilde G_T\succeq0$, we have $|z_{n,T}^\top G_{ns,T}z_{s,T}|^2
\le
(z_{n,T}^\top G_{nn,T}z_{n,T})
(z_{s,T}^\top G_{ss,T}z_{s,T}),$
and hence $z_{n,T}^\top G_{ns,T}z_{s,T}\to0.$
Substituting all these limits in \eqref{eq: J_lim}, we get the result.

Finally, let $\gamma>\gamma_\infty$. Then for every fixed $\nu>0$,
$f_\infty(\nu)<\gamma$, so for sufficiently large $T$,
$f_T(\nu)<f_T(\nu_T)=\gamma$. Since $f_T$ is decreasing,
$\nu_T<\nu$, and hence $\nu_T\to0$. Further, $\widetilde S_T(\nu_T)
\succeq\frac{1}{\nu_T}\widetilde M_T
\succeq\frac{1}{\nu_T}\widetilde\Sigma,$
where $\widetilde\Sigma=P^{-1}\Sigma P^{-\top}\succ0$. Thus, $0\le J_T^*
\le
\widetilde x_f^\top\widetilde S_T(\nu_T)^{-1}\widetilde x_f
\le
\nu_T\widetilde x_f^\top
\widetilde\Sigma^{-1}\widetilde x_f
\to0,$
which proves the second case of result.
\qed

label: lem:block_separation
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: \emph{Asymptotic Block Separation

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\widetilde\Sigma\succ0$ and
$|\lambda_i(A_n)|\ge1$, we have $\lambda_{\min}(M_{nn,T})\to\infty.$

Hence for $\mathcal A_T(\nu)
=
G_{nn,T}+\frac{1}{\nu}M_{nn,T}
\succeq
\frac{1}{\nu}M_{nn,T},$ we obtain $\mathcal A_T(\nu)^{-1}\to0$.
For $\rho(A_s)<1$, all stable-mode
Gramian series converge, and therefore $G_{ss,T}\to W_c^s,$ $M_{ss,T}\to W_w^s,$
Next, for fixed $K<T$,  we write $\mathcal B_T=\mathcal B_T^{(K)}+\mathcal R_T^{(K)}.$
Therefore $\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}\mathcal B_T\|
\le
\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}\mathcal B_T^{(K)}\|
+
\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}\mathcal R_T^{(K)}\|.$
$\mathcal B_T^{(K)}$ is bounded and
$\mathcal A_T^{-1}\to0$, hence the first term vanishes. Moreover, using 
positive semidefiniteness of the tail block, we get $\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}\mathcal R_T^{(K)}\|^2
\le
\|\mathcal D_{T,\mathrm{tail}}^{(K)}\|.$

Since $\rho(A_s)<1$, $\sup_{T>K}\|\mathcal D_{T,\mathrm{tail}}^{(K)}\|\to0
,(K\to\infty).$
Therefore, $\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}\mathcal B_T\|\to0.$ Finally, $\|\mathcal B_T^\top\mathcal A_T^{-1}x_f^n\|
\le
\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}\mathcal B_T\|
\|\mathcal A_T^{-1/2}x_f^n\|
\to0.$ This completes the proof.
\qed
